subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: AC#3 NOT MET — live_preview is dead code. setCommonConfig destructures `live_preview` and calls `(query as any).addParam({ preview_hash: previewHash })` (lines ~131-136), but NONE of the public functions (getEntry, getSingleEntry, getAllContentTypeEntries, findSingletonEntry, getSingletonEntry) destructure or forward `live_preview` to createContentTypeQuery/createContentTypeEntryQuery. They all use explicit destructuring (e.g., `{ contentTypeUid, referenceFieldPath, jsonRtePath, only, lang, includeFields }`) without a rest operator, so `live_preview` is silently dropped at every call site. The setCommonConfig live_preview handling is unreachable dead code — preview context can never flow through to Contentstack queries, directly contradicting AC#3 and prior review feedback: 'query config interfaces lack live_preview fields to forward preview context through to Contentstack queries'.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `live_preview` to the destructuring of each public function and forward it to createContentTypeQuery/createContentTypeEntryQuery. For example, in getEntry: `export const getEntry = async <T>({ contentTypeUid, referenceFieldPath, jsonRtePath, only, lang, includeFields, live_preview }: IContentstackGetEntry): Promise<T> => {` and add `live_preview` to the `factory.createContentTypeQuery({...})` call. Repeat for getSingleEntry, getAllContentTypeEntries, findSingletonEntry, getSingletonEntry. The interfaces already extend ICommonContentstackConfig (which now has live_preview), so the type allows it — the functions just need to forward it.

issues.description: No test verifies that live_preview context actually flows through a public function (getEntry, getSingleEntry, etc.) to the Contentstack query's addParam method. The 4 new tests only check the `options` object and `setHost` behavior. Since the forwarding code in setCommonConfig is dead code (see blocker above), no test can catch this regression. A test that calls getEntry (or similar) with a live_preview parameter and asserts that the mock's `addParam` method was called with `{ preview_hash: <value> }` is required to prove AC#3 is met.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a test such as: `it('should forward live_preview.preview_hash to query.addParam via getEntry', async () => { const addParamSpy = jest.spyOn(Stack, 'addParam' as any); await getEntry({ contentTypeUid: 'contentType', lang: ContentstackLocales.EN, live_preview: { preview_hash: 'test_hash_123' } }); expect(addParamSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ preview_hash: 'test_hash_123' }); });`

issues.description: The `addParam({ preview_hash: previewHash })` call passes a single object argument. The Contentstack delivery SDK's `addParam` method on Query/Entry typically accepts `(key: string, value: string)` as two separate arguments, not a single object. If the SDK expects two args, this will silently fail to set the preview hash on the query. Since the SDK's `.d.ts` doesn't expose `addParam` (hence the `as any` cast), the actual runtime signature cannot be verified from types alone.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify the Contentstack SDK's `addParam` runtime signature. If it accepts `(key, value)`, change to `(query as any).addParam('preview_hash', previewHash)`. If it accepts an object, leave as-is but add a comment citing the SDK source.

issues.description: ILivePreviewConfig includes `enable` and `preview_type` fields which are never used in the query-forwarding path (setCommonConfig only reads `preview_hash`). `enable` belongs on the SDK config (options object), not on the query config interface. Including it here is misleading — callers might set `enable` on the query config thinking it toggles preview, but it would be ignored.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `enable` and `preview_type` from ILivePreviewConfig unless they are actually used in query forwarding. Keep only `preview_hash?: string`.
